content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

content.thinking:
I'm looking at this axial limb slice, trying to figure out the anatomy — there's a bright heterogeneous mass posteriorly with a dark rim that could be a pseudo-capsule around a tumor, and I'm puzzling over whether that darker round structure represents bone given the positioning.

Checking the available marks in that region — 526, 469, 498, 499, 497 — the center of the mass maps roughly to (390,540) on the left panel, corresponding to (1165,540) on the right. Mark 499 sits closest at (1167,544), so I'll go with that one.

content.text:
The bright, lobulated mass with a dark rim in the posterior part of the slice looks like the tumor. Its centre is at roughly x=1165, y=540 in the marked panel, and mark 499 at (1167, 544) lies almost exactly there. I identified the mass by its appearance and did not confirm it against any other cue.

ANSWER: 499
